speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Regarding the rash on your left dorsal hand, has it appeared suddenly or developed gradually, and does it change color or texture during the day? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. The CBC results are normal, which helps rule out acute infection. Given your history of sunbathing, does the rash on your left dorsal hand appear as tight, shiny skin with reduced hair growth and wrinkling, or is it more blistering and painful? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Porokeratosis of Mibelli (acral type).

The description of a "rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque" on the sun-exposed dorsal hand, combined with your history of frequent sunbathing and the absence of pain or tenderness, is highly suggestive of this condition. Can you confirm if you have noticed a raised, ridge-like border (cornoid lamella) surrounding the center of the lesion? REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy_Left_Dorsal_Hand
